findings.summary: The concept-icon strip at the bottom of the cover slide is cut off by the page edge, truncating its labels and captions.
findings.evidence: First label renders as "Images &" with its second line sliced in half at the bottom border, and the caption row beneath it ("…build recipe…", "…hold data…", "…the DNS…", "…one command…") is clipped to a sliver of letter tops.
findings.fix: Reduce the cover block's vertical stack (title/subtitle/note spacing) or drop the bottom icon strip on slide 1 so the full two-line label plus caption fits inside the safe area.

findings.summary: The Container Internals chapter summary is placed on page 4, before the chapter's own sections 5 (example) and 6 (mistakes) which run on page 5.
findings.evidence: Page 4 ends with the checkbox summary "container = ==namespaces== (isolation) + ==cgroups== (limits) + ==overlay== layers (filesystem)" … "Defaults drop caps and filter syscalls; kernel is still shared", yet page 5 then opens "5. Example: the PID 1 problem" and continues "6. Mistakes".
findings.fix: Move the checkbox summary block from the end of page 4 to the end of page 5, after the "6. Mistakes" bullets and the Container vs VM table, so the chapter closes with its summary.

findings.summary: A mistakes bullet relies on Dockerfile `CMD` and shell vs exec form, which are not introduced until pages 9–10.
findings.evidence: Page 5, "6. Mistakes": "Shipping a shell-form CMD as PID 1: signals never reach the app" — `CMD` and shell form are first defined on page 9 ("Shell form `RUN apt-get ...` wraps in `/bin/sh -c`") and page 10 ("`CMD` = default command…").
findings.fix: Reword the bullet to stay inside what the reader knows, e.g. "Starting the app via `sh -c ...` so the shell is PID 1: signals stop at the shell and never reach your app (Dockerfile `CMD` forms, page 10)".

findings.summary: Section 4's heading promises multi-arch coverage, but the multi-arch material only appears on page 7 after section 5 (Common Mistakes).
findings.evidence: Page 6 heading "4. Inspect, Clean, Multi-arch" is followed only by a table of `docker images`, `docker image inspect`, `docker history`, `docker rmi`, `docker image prune`; the "Multi-arch: one tag, many platforms" flowchart (`docker buildx --platform` → manifest list → amd64/arm64) sits on page 7, after page 6's "5. Common Mistakes".
findings.fix: Either move the multi-arch flowchart plus a one-line manifest-list explanation up under heading 4 on page 6 (pushing the mistakes block to page 7), or retitle heading 4 "4. Inspect and Clean" and give the page 7 diagram its own "5. Multi-arch Images" heading before the mistakes section.

findings.summary: The hashtag #kubernetes names an orchestration technology that the series never covers.
findings.evidence: hashtags include "#kubernetes"; the caption scopes the series as "from namespaces and cgroups to Compose, registries and production hardening" and no title mentions Kubernetes or orchestration beyond Compose
findings.fix: Replace #kubernetes with a tag matching actual coverage, e.g. #linuxcontainers or #devopsengineer.

findings.summary: The "fork + exec" label in the Docker Engine Architecture diagram is crossed by the connector line it annotates.
findings.evidence: Label renders as "fork-+-exec" with the horizontal connector running straight through the glyphs.
findings.fix: Offset the edge label a few pixels above the connector, or give it an opaque background fill so the line is masked behind the text.

findings.summary: "Namespaces" is used as the explanation of container isolation in the VM comparison table before it is defined on page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 2 table row "Isolation | strong, heavy | namespaces, light"; the definition "Own view: pids, net, mounts, hostname" and the namespace table only arrive on page 3.
findings.fix: Change the cell to "kernel namespaces (next page), light" or "per-process kernel views, light" so the term is signposted rather than assumed.

findings.summary: Lifecycle commands `docker exec` and `docker stats` are used as known on pages 3–4, but are only defined in the Container Lifecycle chapter on page 8.
findings.evidence: Page 3 mistakes: "Running `sshd` inside; use `docker exec` instead"; page 4 code note: "docker stats web  # live usage" — page 8 is where "`docker exec -it web sh`   # new shell" and "`cp` / `stats` … copy files / live CPU, RAM" are introduced.
findings.fix: Gloss both at first use — "use `docker exec` (open a shell in a running container, page 8) instead" and "`docker stats` shows live CPU/memory, page 8".

findings.summary: `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE` is described as granting only port 80, but it grants binding to every privileged port below 1024.
findings.fix: Reword to "keeps only the right to bind privileged ports (<1024), e.g. 80 and 443".

findings.summary: `throttled_time` is the cgroup v1 field name, but the notes otherwise assume cgroup v2 (which exposes `throttled_usec`), so the named counter will not exist on a modern host.
findings.evidence: "CPU over cap: throttled, not killed; watch `throttled_time`" — while page 5 tells the reader to `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max`, a cgroup v2 path
findings.fix: Use the v2 name: "watch `nr_throttled` / `throttled_usec` in `cpu.stat` (`throttled_time` on cgroup v1)".

findings.summary: The PID 1 / zombie-reaping bullets sit in an unlabelled block between section 4 and the summary, split from their numbered section heading on the next page.
findings.evidence: Page 4 has "4. Capabilities, seccomp, AppArmor" and then an unheaded purple bullet block starting "Kernel gives PID 1 no default signal handlers: `SIGTERM` is ==ignored== unless handled"; the matching heading "5. Example: the PID 1 problem" only appears at the top of page 5.
findings.fix: Add the heading "5. The PID 1 problem" above that purple bullet block on page 4 and retitle the page 5 heading to "5. Example: `--init` and tini", so the concept and its example share one numbered section.

findings.summary: The "rootfs" edge label in the "Anatomy of a running container" diagram is overlapped by the arrow descending from runc (OCI).
findings.evidence: "rootfs" appears with the vertical arrow shaft drawn through the middle of the word, under the "runc (OCI)" node.
findings.fix: Shift the "rootfs" label clear of the arrow path (or add an opaque label background) so the stroke does not cross the text.

findings.summary: Heading "5. Common Mistakes" already appears on page 3.
findings.fix: Fine if the two pages cover different topics; rename if they do not.

findings.summary: The pinning tip points at `docker image inspect` without saying which digest to copy; its `.Id` field is the local config digest and is not usable as `nginx@sha256:...`.
findings.evidence: "for exact reproducibility copy the digest from `docker image inspect` and run `nginx@sha256:...`"
findings.fix: Name the field: `docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' nginx:1.27` (the repo digest, not `.Id`).

findings.summary: The claim that `docker logs` captures only PID 1's output is wrong — it captures anything written to the container's stdout/stderr, including child processes that inherit those descriptors.
findings.fix: Change to "logs capture whatever is written to the container's stdout/stderr (PID 1 and any child that inherits them); output written to files inside the container is invisible".
